group_results.reason: The new parent-key parameter supports the nested-object diagnostic, but the target only enters object unpacking at the root with a NULL parent key.
A wrong-type nested object can produce a key-specific diagnostic, but no existing format asks for a nested object.
The changed object-child call propagates a key, but the only object-child format in the target is permissive 'o', which performs no wrong-type check.
The key-specific array wrong-type diagnostic requires an array-valued object field; the target checks for an array only at an already-array root.
For an input array, the existing '[o!]' call reaches array-element unpacking, which passes NULL as the element's key.
The dispatcher supports key-specific string mismatch diagnostics, but none of the target's formats selects 's' as a value type.
The key-specific 'i' mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests an integer object field.
The key-specific 'I' mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests a json_int_t object field.
The key-specific boolean mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests a boolean object field.
The key-specific real mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests an 'f' object field.
The key-specific real-or-integer mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests an 'F' object field.
The key-specific null mismatch is unreachable because the target never requests an 'n' object field.
Every existing json_unpack call reaches json_vunpack_ex, which supplies NULL for the top-level key.
This change adds API-suite checks for the diagnostics. It changes neither this fuzz entry nor a source behavior it invokes.

build.reason: The supplied build entry delegates to test/ossfuzz/ossfuzz.sh, whose contents are absent. The supplied Makefile lists and links this target, but does not establish how the delegated script invokes it.

input.reason: A finite input can provide a selector byte and valid JSON object, such as {"data":42}; json_loadb accepts the bounded buffer and the target proceeds when parsing succeeds.

lifecycle.reason: The target releases its copied and parsed JSON values and dump buffer. Its 'o' outputs are borrowed values and are not used after the root is released.

control_flow.reason: The fixed formats enter the unpack dispatcher, but the only object-field format is optional 'o'. No input byte can select a type-enforcing nested format, so the new keyed wrong-type behaviors remain unreachable.

accepted.requirement: Object-field unpacking must reach the supported wrong-type diagnostic for a nested object with its field key.
accepted.target_route: Parsed object -> json_unpack -> json_vunpack_ex -> unpack_object -> field unpack -> nested unpack_object.
accepted.failure_condition: With input containing {"data":42}, the target calls '{s?o}' for data. Its 'o' child accepts the integer; no nested-object type check is reached.
accepted.alternative_paths: Top-level 'o' accepts any value; '[o!]' runs only for an array root and also uses 'o'. The selector byte changes dump flags, not unpack formats.

accepted.requirement: Object-field unpacking must reach the supported wrong-type diagnostic for an expected nested array with its field key.
accepted.target_route: Parsed object -> object-field unpack -> '[' dispatch -> unpack_array with parent_key.
accepted.failure_condition: For {"data":42}, the target's '{s?o}' accepts data. Its '[o!]' format is only called when the root already passes json_is_array.
accepted.alternative_paths: The root-array path has a NULL parent key; the other two formats do not request an array field.

accepted.alternative_paths: Top-level 'o' and array '[o!]' do not select string value dispatch.
